briefing.opening: Good day, everyone. We will now begin today's climate briefing, November 10, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 The Climate Crisis: A Shadow Cast Over Daily Life and Ecosystems
sections.content: Several reports released today clearly demonstrate that the climate crisis is no longer a distant future concern but is directly impacting our lives and ecosystems. Notably, 92% of Gyeonggi Province residents report experiencing climate change, with significant concerns about health impacts. Health disparities are becoming a reality, with vulnerable populations experiencing heat-related illnesses at a rate of 46.5% [2, 3, 12, 14, 16, 22, 24, 26]. The UN has warned that this climate crisis constitutes a 'pandemic-scale' health emergency [82], and the UNFCCC Executive Secretary likened fossil fuels to 'cancer,' stating they spread global inflation [10, 107, 120]. Furthermore, severe impacts on ecosystems are being detected, such as a deepening sex ratio imbalance with female sea turtles exceeding 70% [13]. Concerns have also been raised that global warming could be progressing faster than anticipated due to blind spots in climate models [21, 81, 93, 108].

sections.title: 🌍 COP31 Opens: Fossil Fuel Debate and Call for Global Action
sections.content: Following a year of catastrophic extreme weather, the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference of the Parties (COP31) has opened in Antalya, Türkiye [88, 91, 92, 112, 116, 121]. Key issues at this conference are expected to include the question of climate change cost payments and whether fossil fuels can be explicitly named as the cause of the climate emergency [96, 111, 122]. While there was a trend of the U.S. not attending COP31, the Democratic Party, energized by the midterm elections, is set to participate in the talks, emphasizing the promotion of clean energy [87, 98, 106]. Meanwhile, the UNFCCC's '2026 Global Climate Action Yearbook' revealed implementation gaps in six key areas despite tangible achievements [18]. Australia's Climate Change Minister emphasized that achieving the 1.5°C target remains possible, urging efforts from the international community [118].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Technological and Policy Progress Towards Carbon Neutrality and Adaptation
sections.content: News of various domestic and international efforts and technological innovations to address the climate crisis also continued. KIST is strengthening climate change adaptation research by establishing a 'Forest Climate Change Testbed' that simulates 'future heatwaves' [4, 6, 7]. The Rural Development Administration (RDA) is making adaptation efforts in the agricultural sector, including discussing mycotoxin safety management strategies and researching customized rice varieties to respond to climate change [8, 9, 11]. The carbon neutrality achievements of domestic companies and public institutions have also been notable, with Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO), Korea Midland Power (KOMIPO), Techross, and Gangnam-gu City Management Corporation, among others, receiving presidential and ministerial commendations at the Carbon Neutrality and Green Management Awards [15, 31, 36, 37, 40, 42, 44, 45]. Additionally, local governments such as Yeonggwang-gun and Gwangmyeong-si are spreading carbon neutrality practices in daily life through village leader training and community festivals [30, 35, 47]. Yeosu City is making an all-out effort to host COP33 [5, 20].

sections.title: ⚡️ Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition, Shaping a New Energy Landscape
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is accelerating, signaling significant changes in the energy landscape. The Ministry of Climate has recognized seven new types of hydrothermal energy sources, including leaked groundwater, sewage/wastewater, and industrial water, as renewable energy sources. This is expected to enable heating supply to 3 million households using discarded water [49, 63, 64, 68, 76, 78]. Domestic local governments, such as Inje-gun and Daejeon City, are actively leading the dissemination of new and renewable energy and fostering the solar power industry [50, 51, 54, 59, 60, 73, 75]. Global renewable energy capacity is projected to surge to 4800 GW, and the integration of renewable energy and AI technology is accelerating [52, 55]. The sharp rise in oil and gas prices due to the Iran war is acting as a factor that slightly reduces greenhouse gas emissions from fossil fuel use and further accelerates the renewable energy transition [119, 123].

briefing.closing: As we have seen in today's briefing, the climate crisis demands immediate action and in-depth discussion across all sectors of our society. At the same time, seeds of hope for a sustainable future are being sown through technological innovation and policy efforts. The attention and actions of all of us will be a crucial driving force in overcoming the climate crisis. This concludes today's climate briefing.
